label: History
value: Agatha Sowerby resides at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley.
unit: Agatha Sowerby resides at Sowerby’s Hollow in Brierley, where she keeps a vigilant eye over the main thoroughfare from her kitchen window. On a June afternoon, she notices Obed Abernethy driving out in his finest clothes and buggy, ruined her afternoon by her inability to guess his destination. She visits Grey Shutters after tea and learns from Thirza Abernethy that Obed went to collect an orphan boy from Nova Scotia. Agatha strongly disapproves, warning Thirza of the hazards of taking in an unfamiliar orphan. Later, after recovering from a severe bout of influenza, Agatha visits Grey Shutters to inspect the orphan, who turns out to be a girl named Nell. Agatha blunt remarks about Nell’s plain looks and red hair trigger an explosive outburst of rage from Nell, leaving Agatha appalled. After Thirza demands that Nell apologize, Nell visits Agatha’s house to deliver a dramatic, thorough plea for forgiveness. Touched by the apology, Agatha forgives Nell completely, offers her white June lilies from her garden, and admits her growing fondness for the child.

label: History
value: Barney Pullen resides in Brierley.
unit: Barney Pullen resides in Brierley as the son of Gorham Pullen. During the Sunday-school picnic at his father's field, he assists by taking attendees rowing on the Lake of Glassy Waters and rescues Odette Pullen when she nearly falls into the lake. Later in the summer, he uses his family's double-seated buggy to drive his sister Odette, Isolde Pembroke, and Nell Harcourt to the concert at the Pale Sands Hotel. Though proud to ride alongside Nell on the front seat, his shyness prevents him from holding a conversation with her. Upon arriving at the hotel, he flees out of fear of being invited to the performers' dinner, but reliably waits with his team of horses to drive the girls back home after the event.

label: History
value: Belinda came to live at Echo Cottage at the age of thirteen.
unit: Belinda came to live at Echo Cottage at the age of thirteen to assist Miss Rosalind Penrose with domestic chores, becoming the fourth in a succession of Bowman sisters to hold the position and accept the moniker 'Belinda.' During the visit of Nell and Isolde to Echo Cottage, she dutifully assisted her mistress with entertaining and managing the household, despite a propensity for breaking chinaware. When Miss Penrose's former suitor, Stephen Stanhope, returned to court her, Belinda eagerly supported the romance. Following Miss Penrose's wedding to Stephen Stanhope at Echo Cottage, Belinda prepared to relocate to Boston with the newlyweds to continue serving them.

label: History
value: Cedric Stanhope was born in the United States.
unit: Cedric Stanhope was born in the United States and lost his mother when he was three years old. He was raised by his father, Stephen Stanhope, in Boston until he was sent to live with his grandmother on St. Brendan's Island in Brierley. There, he attended the Brierley school under Nell Harcourt. During a winter night when Posy Fay Pembroke fell ill with croup, Cedric ran to Brierley to summon help and assisted Nell in nursing the child through the night. Later, when Nell fell ill with a severe ankle injury, Cedric visited her faithfully and comforted her. In school, he proved to be an intelligent and popular student who formed a special bond of kindred friendship with Nell, sharing his whimsical daydreams with her.

label: History
value: Hugh spent several years in Alberta.
unit: Hugh spent several years in Alberta due to his father's illness, returning to Brierley after lacking regular schooling. During the summer before his return to Brierley school, he visited cousins in New Brunswick. Upon returning to class in the fourth book, he pulled a prank on Opal Pettigrew by tying her hair to her chair and teased the new student, Nell Harcourt, by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots'. In response, Nell smashed her slate over his head. Hugh bravely admitted to the schoolmaster, Mr. Pidgeon, that he had provoked her. After school, Hugh tried to apologize to Nell for mocking her hair, but she snubbed him. When Mr. Pidgeon later forced Nell to sit next to Hugh as a punishment for being late, Hugh tried to offer her a candy heart, which she crushed under her shoe. Later in the school year, Hugh performed a recitation of 'Bingen on the Rhine' at the Debating Club concert and picked up a rose that dropped from Nell's hair. Hugh competed fiercely with Nell for top academic marks in the fifth class, excelling in geometry, spelling, and arithmetic.

Upon returning to class in the fourth book, he pulled a prank on Opal Pettigrew by tying her hair to her chair and teased the new student, Nell Harcourt, by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots'. In response, Nell smashed her slate over his head. Hugh bravely admitted to the schoolmaster, Mr. Pidgeon, that he had provoked her. After school, Hugh tried to apologize to Nell for mocking her hair, but she snubbed him. When Mr. Pidgeon later forced Nell to sit next to Hugh as a punishment for being late, Hugh tried to offer her a candy heart, which she crushed under her shoe. Later in the school year, Hugh performed a recitation of 'Bingen on the Rhine' at the Debating Club concert and picked up a rose that dropped from Nell's hair. Hugh competed fiercely with Nell for top academic marks in the fifth class, excelling in geometry, spelling, and arithmetic.

label: History
value: Isolde grows up at Pear Hill
unit: Isolde grows up at Pear Hill in Brierley and becomes the bosom friend of Nell Harcourt shortly after Nell's arrival at Grey Shutters. The two girls swear an oath of lifelong loyalty over a imaginary stream in the Pembroke garden and establish a playhouse called Larkrise. When Isolde accidentally consumes homemade currant wine instead of raspberry cordial at Grey Shutters and returns home unwell, her mother forbids her from playing with Nell, leading to a tearful temporary farewell between the friends. After Nell helps care for Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay during an attack of croup, Mrs. Pembroke forgives Nell and allows the girls to resume their friendship. Isolde attends Brierley school alongside Nell, participating in school plays, concerts, the story club, and the Brierley Village Improvement Society. Later, she supports Nell through her academic pursuits and entrance examinations at Regent's Academy.

unit: Isolde grows up at Pear Hill in Brierley and becomes the bosom friend of Nell Harcourt shortly after Nell's arrival at Grey Shutters. The two girls swear an oath of lifelong loyalty over a imaginary stream in the Pembroke garden and establish a playhouse called Larkrise. When Isolde accidentally consumes homemade currant wine instead of raspberry cordial at Grey Shutters and returns home unwell, her mother forbids her from playing with Nell, leading to a tearful temporary farewell between the friends. After Nell helps care for Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay during an attack of croup, Mrs. Pembroke forgives Nell and allows the girls to resume their friendship. Isolde attends Brierley school alongside Nell, participating in school plays, concerts, the story club, and the Brierley Village Improvement Society. Later, she supports Nell through her academic pursuits and entrance examinations at Regent's Academy.

label: History
value: Isolde Pembroke lived at Pear Hill.
unit: Isolde Pembroke lived at Pear Hill near Pembroke's Pond with her parents and sisters. After returning from a visit to her aunt in Delford, she met Nell Harcourt in the family garden at the suggestion of her mother. The two girls quickly hit it off and swore a solemn vow of lifelong friendship over the garden path. Isolde accompanied Nell and Thirza Abernethy partway home to Grey Shutters and shared chocolates given by Obed. She later constructed a playhouse called Larkrise in a nearby birch grove with Nell, where they played with china fragments and a 'fairy glass'. Isolde also offered to teach Nell songs and share books with her.

value: Nell is intensely imaginative.
unit: Nell is an intensely imaginative, romantic, and loquacious girl with a passionate, fiery temper that flares up quickly when her looks or red hair are insulted. Deeply sensitive to beauty and affection, she feels emotions acutely, plunging into despair over disappointments and soaring into ecstasy over simple joys. She possesses a lively wit, a dramatic flair, and an earnest desire to be good, though her impulsive nature and vivid daydreams often lead her into unexpected blunders and scrapes. Despite her sensitivity, she is courageous, forgiving, and intensely loyal to her friends and foster family.

label: History
value: Nell was brought to Brierley by mistake instead of a boy.
unit: Brought to Brierley by mistake instead of a boy, Nell quickly won over Obed Abernethy and eventually his sister Thirza, who decided to keep her at Grey Shutters. She settled into the community, naming local landmarks with imaginative titles, making a bosom friend in Isolde Pembroke, and entering Brierley School. Her early years at Grey Shutters were marked by energetic scrapes, including an outburst at neighbor Agatha Sowerby over her red hair, accidentally getting Isolde drunk on homemade currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, and confessing to stealing a brooch she had merely misplaced. At school, she engaged in a fierce academic rivalry with Hugh Carrow, which escalated into a slate-smashing incident after he mocked her hair. She subsequently left school briefly in protest of the teacher's punishment, but returned and successfully advanced to the higher grades. Nell excelled academically and socially, organizing a story club and performing in local concerts. She settled into the community, naming local landmarks with imaginative titles, making a bosom friend in Isolde Pembroke, and entering Brierley School. Her early years at Grey Shutters were marked by energetic scrapes, including an outburst at neighbor Agatha Sowerby over her red hair, accidentally getting Isolde drunk on homemade currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, and confessing to stealing a brooch she had merely misplaced. At school, she engaged in a fierce academic rivalry with Hugh Carrow, which escalated into a slate-smashing incident after he mocked her hair. She subsequently left school briefly in protest of the teacher's punishment, but returned and successfully advanced to the higher grades. Nell excelled academically and socially, organizing a story club and performing in local concerts. When Obed Abernethy died suddenly following the failure of the Abbey Bank, Nell gave up an opportunity to attend college immediately and took up teaching at Brierley School to support Thirza and keep Grey Shutters. During her time teaching, she saved the life of little Posy Fay Pembroke during an attack of croup, helped establish the Brierley Village Improvement Society, and accidentally dyed her hair green before cutting it short. Later, after winning the Avery Scholarship at Regent's Academy in Portmaris, she earned her First Class teacher's license and pursued an Arts degree at Wexcombe College alongside friends Honora Hollis, Mabel Colby, and Cressida Lindsay, residing at Tabby's Place. After resolving her lingering grudges with Hugh Carrow, Nell realized her true love for him, rejected a marriage proposal from Cyril Lisle, and eventually accepted Hugh's proposal in Dinah Wren's old garden. She gave up her scholarship to stay at Grey Shutters when Thirza's eyesight began to fail, taking the local teaching position in Brierley after Hugh selflessly yielded it to her.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy grew up at Grey Shutters.
unit: Obed Abernethy grew up at Grey Shutters, a farmstead set far back from the main thoroughfare in Brierley. Due to advancing age and heart trouble, he and his sister Thirza arranged through Mrs. Alexander Tranter to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to assist with farm work. However, when Obed drove the sorrel mare to Alder River station to meet the train, he found that a young girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent by mistake instead. Though bewildered and timid, Obed drove Nell back to Grey Shutters, enjoying her loquacious chatter along the way. Upon arriving, Thirza initially insisted on returning Nell to the asylum, but Obed developed a fondness for the girl and quietly advocated for keeping her. Despite Thirza taking her to Pale Sands to arrange her return or reassignment, Obed hired a local French boy for farm labor in hopes of keeping Nell. His quiet determination eventually persuaded Thirza to let Nell stay. When Nell was later confined to her room for refusing to apologize to Agatha Sowerby, Obed secretly tiptoed upstairs to comfort her and gently persuaded her to apologize. He later bought chocolate sweeties for Nell in Delford, delighting her and cementing their warm bond.

However, when Obed drove the sorrel mare to Alder River station to meet the train, he found that a young girl, Nell Harcourt, had been sent by mistake instead. Though bewildered and timid, Obed drove Nell back to Grey Shutters, enjoying her loquacious chatter along the way. Upon arriving, Thirza initially insisted on returning Nell to the asylum, but Obed developed a fondness for the girl and quietly advocated for keeping her. Despite Thirza taking her to Pale Sands to arrange her return or reassignment, Obed hired a local French boy for farm labor in hopes of keeping Nell. His quiet determination eventually persuaded Thirza to let Nell stay. When Nell was later confined to her room for refusing to apologize to Agatha Sowerby, Obed secretly tiptoed upstairs to comfort her and gently persuaded her to apologize. He later bought chocolate sweeties for Nell in Delford, delighting her and cementing their warm bond.

She is honest and straightforward, often expressing her opinions directly and lacking interest in flowery or creative imaginings. Despite her lack of imagination, she is good-natured, supportive of her friends, and very reliable. She approaches work and studies diligently, aiming to fulfill her duties and satisfy authorities rather than seeking grand ideals or fame.

label: History
value: Odette grew up in Brierley.
unit: Odette grew up in Brierley, studying at the local school alongside her peers. In her late teens, she prepared for the entrance examination for Regent's Academy under the guidance of Mr. Pidgeon and later Miss Agnes Thorne. She joined the student Story Club, writing sensible and realistic stories, and actively participated in school concerts and events. After successfully passing the Entrance examinations, she attended Regent's Academy in Portmaris with Nell Harcourt, Opal Pettigrew, and others. Upon completing her Second Class work, she secured a position as a schoolteacher in Stonebridge, intending to dedicate her life to pedagogy and financial independence.

label: History
value: Opal attended Brierley school.
unit: Opal attended Brierley school, where she sat in the fourth and fifth books alongside Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke. She joined the school's story-writing club, where she gained a reputation for writing overly sentimental stories. After finishing school, she studied for the entrance examinations for Regent's Academy alongside her classmates and participated in a student concert, acting in the tableau 'Grace, Hope and Charity.' At Regent's Academy, she joined the Brierley student group and passed her examinations, qualifying for a First Class teaching license. Following a severe bout of congestion during her final winter at college, Opal's health rapidly declined into galloping consumption, preventing her from taking a teaching position at Pale Sands. She spent her final summer at her family's home in Brierley, continually denying the severity of her illness while remaining obsessed with her various suitors. After a frank, emotional conversation about her fears of death with Nell, Opal passed away peacefully in her sleep toward the end of summer.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer moved from New Brunswick to Brierley.
unit: Mr. Pettifer moved from New Brunswick to Brierley, purchasing the farm previously owned by Robert Bell. He earned an immediate reputation among locals for his eccentric household habits, short temper, and his cursing parrot, Nutmeg. When his neighbor's Jersey cow repeatedly trespassed into his oat field, he confronted Nell Harcourt in a rage. After realizing his own fence was in poor condition and admitting his hasty temper, he reconciled with Nell and accepted her offer of a home-baked nut cake. Later, when Nell mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow thinking it was her own, she confessed to him and offered her own cow in trade; Mr. Pettifer accepted the trade in good humor and hosted Nell for tea. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife, Emily, arrived unexpectedly at his home, having learned of false rumors that he was seeking a new wife. Reunited with Emily and relieved of his parrot after its death during a lightning storm, Mr. Pettifer settled into a clean, orderly life with her.

unit: Mr. Pettifer moved from New Brunswick to Brierley, purchasing the farm previously owned by Robert Bell. He earned an immediate reputation among locals for his eccentric household habits, short temper, and his cursing parrot, Nutmeg. When his neighbor's Jersey cow repeatedly trespassed into his oat field, he confronted Nell Harcourt in a rage. After realizing his own fence was in poor condition and admitting his hasty temper, he reconciled with Nell and accepted her offer of a home-baked nut cake. Later, when Nell mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow thinking it was her own, she confessed to him and offered her own cow in trade; Mr. Pettifer accepted the trade in good humor and hosted Nell for tea. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife, Emily, arrived unexpectedly at his home, having learned of false rumors that he was seeking a new wife. Reunited with Emily and relieved of his parrot after its death during a lightning storm, Mr. Pettifer settled into a clean, orderly life with her.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon serves as the schoolmaster at the Brierley school.
unit: Mr. Pidgeon serves as the schoolmaster at the Brierley school, where he spends much of his time assisting the sixteen-year-old Sukey Pullen with her studies and attempting to court her. During lessons, he frequently ignores the younger children or writes romantic notes and poetry. On one occasion, after Hugh Carrow teases Nell Harcourt about her red hair, causing her to smash her slate over Hugh's head, Mr. Pidgeon disciplines Nell by forcing her to stand at the blackboard and writing a derogatory note about her temper above her head. Later, when a group of students arrives late after picking spruce gum, he singles out Nell as a victim and forces her to sit next to Hugh Carrow. Deeply insulted by his treatment, Nell refuses to return to school for the remainder of the term. At the Debating Club concert in Mr. Gorham Pullen's field, Mr. Pidgeon delivers a moving recitation of Mark Antony's address above the body of Caesar, directing his emotional delivery toward Sukey Pullen.

On one occasion, after Hugh Carrow teases Nell Harcourt about her red hair, causing her to smash her slate over Hugh's head, Mr. Pidgeon disciplines Nell by forcing her to stand at the blackboard and writing a derogatory note about her temper above her head. Later, when a group of students arrives late after picking spruce gum, he singles out Nell as a victim and forces her to sit next to Hugh Carrow. Deeply insulted by his treatment, Nell refuses to return to school for the remainder of the term. At the Debating Club concert in Mr. Gorham Pullen's field, Mr. Pidgeon delivers a moving recitation of Mark Antony's address above the body of Caesar, directing his emotional delivery toward Sukey Pullen.

label: History
value: Robin grew up as a twin.
unit: Robin grew up as a twin in a large family in Nova Scotia under the care of Mrs. Rudge and Nell Harcourt. Following the death of his father and later his mother, Mary Farrow, Robin and his twin sister Lucy were taken in by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters in Brierley. Shortly after his arrival, his constant restless energy and penchant for pranks caused frequent chaos, including dropping a live caterpillar down Lauretta White's collar during church and tricking his sister Lucy into walking a pigpen fence. Though often punished by being sent to bed or denied meals, he continually proved to be resilient, affectionate, and cheerful. Over time, Robin started attending the local school and developed a fierce rivalrous desire to emulate or outdo Cedric Stanhope in good behavior and height. He also formed a close friendship with Mr. Pettifer, whom he assisted in farm chores like hauling dulse.

label: History
value: Rosalind Penrose was betrothed to Stephen Stanhope.
unit: In her youth, Rosalind Penrose was betrothed to Stephen Stanhope. Following a misunderstanding and an argument driven by her pride, their engagement ended and Stephen departed for the United States, leaving her heartbroken. Refusing to love or marry anyone else, she lived a quiet, secluded life for twenty-five years in her sandstone home, Echo Cottage, entertaining herself with her imagination, her echoes, and a series of young maidservants whom she called 'Belinda'. She eventually met Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke when they stumbled upon her garden, forming a warm friendship with them. Nell later introduced her to Stephen's son, Cedric. Hearing of Stephen's return, Nell arranged for Stephen to visit her at Echo Cottage. The two reconciled, leading to their marriage in her garden beneath a honeysuckle arbor. Afterward, she departed with Stephen for a journey to the Pacific coast, planning to reside in Boston while keeping Echo Cottage for summer visits.

unit: In her youth, Rosalind Penrose was betrothed to Stephen Stanhope. Following a misunderstanding and an argument driven by her pride, their engagement ended and Stephen departed for the United States, leaving her heartbroken. Refusing to love or marry anyone else, she lived a quiet, secluded life for twenty-five years in her sandstone home, Echo Cottage, entertaining herself with her imagination, her echoes, and a series of young maidservants whom she called 'Belinda'. She eventually met Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke when they stumbled upon her garden, forming a warm friendship with them. Nell later introduced her to Stephen's son, Cedric. Hearing of Stephen's return, Nell arranged for Stephen to visit her at Echo Cottage. The two reconciled, leading to their marriage in her garden beneath a honeysuckle arbor. Afterward, she departed with Stephen for a journey to the Pacific coast, planning to reside in Boston while keeping Echo Cottage for summer visits.

label: History
value: Thirza Abernethy resides at Grey Shutters.
unit: Thirza Abernethy resides at Grey Shutters with her brother Obed. Having agreed to adopt a young orphan boy to assist on the farm, they are shocked when Obed returns from the station with an eleven-year-old girl named Nell Harcourt instead. Although Thirza initially insists on returning Nell to the asylum, she accompanies Nell to Pale Sands to make arrangements. Upon seeing the woman who might otherwise take Nell, Thirza refuses to surrender the orphan and agrees to keep her at Grey Shutters, taking on the responsibility of raising her. She instructs Nell in homemaking, proper behavior, and religious prayers, attempting to curb the girl's wild imagination and loquacity. When neighbor Agatha Sowerby insults Nell's appearance, causing Nell to fly into a rage, Thirza insists Nell apologize, though she secretly defends Nell's feelings to Agatha. Later, Thirza wrongly accuses Nell of stealing and losing her cherished amethyst brooch, locking Nell in her room until she falsely confesses, only for Thirza to discover the brooch tangled in her own shawl. Over time, Thirza grows deeply attached to Nell, eventually admitting that the girl has brought her a new sense of motherhood and happiness. When Nell refuses to return to school after being humiliated by her teacher, Thirza, on Agatha's advice, allows her to study at home instead. She later supports Nell through her various mishaps, including the accidental intoxication of her friend Isolde with homemade currant wine.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired as the new teacher for the Brierley schoolhouse.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired as the new teacher for the Brierley schoolhouse, becoming the first female teacher employed in the village. Upon taking her position in the autumn, she quickly earned the devotion of her students, including Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow, through her gentle manners, clear explanations, and engaging curriculum.
